title: Reliable and Long-Lasting Ex Vivo Recordings of Sciatic Nerve Activity in Mice

steps.title: Prepare stock solutions and aCSF
steps.instruction: Make the following stock solutions in double‑distilled water (DDW) and filter them: 300 mM KCl (1.12 g/50 mL), 200 mM MgSO₄·7H₂O (2.46 g/50 mL), 125 mM NaH₂PO₄·H₂O (0.86 g/50 mL), 200 mM CaCl₂·2H₂O (1.47 g/50 mL), 1 260 mM NaCl (36.82 g/500 mL), 260 mM NaHCO₃ (10.92 g/500 mL). Store at 4 °C for up to three months. On the day of use, pour 350 mL DDW into a beaker, add the KCl, NaH₂PO₄, MgSO₄, NaCl and NaHCO₃ stocks, then dissolve glucose (0.9008 g for 10 mM). Do NOT add CaCl₂ yet. Oxygenate the solution by bubbling 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ for 30 min. Add CaCl₂ stock (5 mL of 200 mM) and adjust pH to 7.4 with NaOH. Bring the final volume to 500 mL with DDW, keep oxygenated, and keep at room temperature for the experiment.

steps.title: Fabricate three‑compartment chamber
steps.instruction: Day 1: Mark two 10 mm external wells and a central 10 × 20 mm chamber on the bottom of a 60 × 15 mm Petri dish, leaving a 2 mm gap. Weigh 30.8 g Sylgard 184 (≈30 mL) and add 3.8 g silicone elastomer (10 % w/w). Mix gently by inversion (total ≈33.77 g). Place a 10 mm test tube on each external marking, cover openings with parafilm, pour the Sylgard mixture into the dish, and incubate at 37 °C overnight. Day 2: Cut out the central rectangle with a scalpel, remove the piece with forceps, and extract the test tubes to create the lateral wells. Cut a 1 mm groove between wells with a razor blade. Clean the plate with 100 % ethanol. Prepare an insulating Sylgard layer by mixing 5 mL Sylgard 184 with 0.5 mL elastomer (10 %); add a thin layer onto the central chamber and wells using a cut Pasteur pipette.

steps.title: Assemble silver wire electrodes
steps.instruction: For stimulating/recording electrodes: strip 2 mm of insulation from both cable ends, spiral ~1 cm bare silver wire around one stripped end, weld with a lead, cover the joint with a 5 mm shrinkable tube and heat‑shrink with a heat gun, then attach the opposite cable end to a banana connector. Chloride the recording electrode by immersing it overnight in HCl or bleach. For Ag/Cl pellet electrodes: repeat the stripping and spiraling steps using the pellet wire, then hermetically seal the joint with shrinkable tubing.

steps.title: Condition aCSF for dissection
steps.instruction: Bring the prepared aCSF to room temperature and bubble it with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ for 15 min before any surgical work.

steps.title: Prepare dissection tools and petri dish
steps.instruction: Disinfect all surgical instruments (scalpel, scissors, forceps, etc.) and the work surface with 70 % ethanol. Fill a 100 × 15 mm Petri dish with the room‑temperature, oxygenated aCSF; this dish will receive the dissected nerves. The dissection must be completed within 30 min; nerves can be kept in continuously bubbled aCSF at room temperature for up to 6 h.

steps.title: Anesthetize and euthanize mouse
steps.instruction: Inject pentobarbital intraperitoneally at 2000 mg/kg. Confirm loss of hind‑limb withdrawal reflex (pinch) and corneal reflex. Perform decapitation to euthanize.

steps.title: Expose and excise sciatic nerve
steps.instruction: Place the mouse on its side, remove dorsal skin with forceps and sharp scissors. Using a scalpel, cut skin near the sciatic notch to expose the nerve. Slide a #11 scalpel blade along the nerve, marking the nerve side with a surgical marker. Continue cutting through fascia to the distal bifurcation, then cut the distal segment. Follow the nerve proximally to the L3‑L4 spinal insertion, cut the bone notch at a 90° angle, and cut through muscle to expose the proximal end. Section the proximal end (~20 mm length) with Vannas scissors, gently dissect remaining connective tissue without touching the nerve, and transfer the nerve to the aCSF‑filled Petri dish. Repeat on the contralateral side.

steps.title: Clean isolated nerve
steps.instruction: Under a binocular microscope, remove all excess branches, muscle, blood clots and adipose tissue by holding tissue with fine tying forceps and cutting with Vannas scissors, taking care not to touch the nerve itself. Transfer the cleaned nerve to continuously oxygenated aCSF at room temperature.

steps.title: Place nerve in three‑compartment chamber
steps.instruction: Apply a U‑shaped line of heavy‑duty silicone grease to the bottom of each notch. Using jeweler’s forceps, gently slide the distal side of the nerve through the notch from proximal to distal, ensuring no overhang on the proximal side (a slight distal overhang is acceptable). Add additional silicone grease over the notches to secure the nerve, trim any proximal overhang, then fill the lateral wells and central chamber with aCSF. Position the chamber on a heating plate, place stimulating, recording and grounding electrodes, and start perfusion. Warm and oxygenate the nerve for 5–10 min to allow acclimation.

steps.title: Configure amplifier and stimulator
steps.instruction: Set amplifier high‑pass filter to 3 Hz and low‑pass filter to 20 kHz. Use gain = 500 for large‑fiber recordings and gain = 5 000 for C‑fiber recordings. Set the Isoflurax stimulator to deliver square pulses (max 10 mA), positive or negative polarity.

steps.title: Record large‑fiber compound action potentials
steps.instruction: Deliver 0.1 ms square current pulses (positive or negative) with the cathode in the central compartment and anode in a lateral well. Set a baseline delay of ≥1 ms before each pulse. Start with currents from 0.005 to 1 mA, spacing stimuli by ≥200 ms. Determine the supramaximal intensity (evoking 85–90 % of maximal CAP amplitude). For each stimulus record peak amplitude, latency to peak and half‑peak, CAP duration, area under the curve, rise time, excitation threshold and recruitment curve. Calculate conduction velocity using CV = 10 mm / delay (ms) (central chamber length = 10 mm). Typical A‑fiber CAP amplitude: 4–10 mV.

steps.title: Measure large‑fiber refractory period
steps.instruction: Using the supramaximal current, deliver paired pulses and increase the inter‑pulse interval from 0.1 to 10 ms. Record the amplitude of the second CAP at each interval and plot the refractory period curve (absolute and relative refractory periods).

steps.title: Evaluate large‑fiber fatigue
steps.instruction: At supramaximal intensity, apply 100‑ms pulse trains at frequencies of 100, 200, … up to 1 000 Hz, with 0.5 s between trains. Analyze the amplitude of each CAP within a train relative to the first CAP, the change in amplitude with frequency, and the slope of amplitude decline.

steps.title: Record C‑fiber compound action potentials
steps.instruction: Increase amplifier gain to 5 000. Deliver 1 ms square pulses with a baseline delay of ≥10 ms. Use currents from 0.1 to 1 mA, spacing stimuli by ≥1 s. Determine supramaximal response. Record peak amplitude, latency (for conduction velocity) and generate stimulus‑duration/response‑amplitude curves. Typical C‑fiber CAP amplitude: 0.06–0.14 mV.

steps.title: Characterize C‑fiber stimulus‑duration response
steps.instruction: With supramaximal current, vary pulse duration from 0.1 to 1 ms and record the resulting CAP amplitudes. Plot stimulus duration versus response amplitude.
